acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

header.reason: The CFO froze all new vendor projects after a missed Q3, so nobody chose another option. The rep calls it timing, but finance saw the project as a 'nice to have': the customer-specific payback number the champion asked for a month earlier was never built, and the CFO was never reached.

findings.finding: Owen asked for proof of payback and got our general ROI deck, which he said would not work with finance; we need a quick way to build a payback case from the customer's own numbers as soon as finance questions start.
findings.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.
findings.who: Owen (customer VP of Product, via Renee)

findings.finding: We never met the CFO who held the budget and relied on the champion to bring her in at the end; our sales motion needs a finance conversation early, with material written for the CFO.
findings.quote: We only ever talked to product and engineering.

findings.finding: The cost of the homegrown system, including engineering time, billing errors and subscriptions lapsing on failed cards, was raised but never added up; the AE thinks no one told the CFO what it was costing, so our message should name the cost of doing nothing.
Our revenue-growth pitch missed; the buyer described billing as a drag on the roadmap, and the demo of fast pricing changes landed, so lead with roadmap speed for product buyers.
findings.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap.
findings.who: Owen (customer VP of Product, via Renee)

findings.finding: Migration concerns (keeping existing cards, moving in stages, avoiding renewal season) were answered with a doc, but the buyer wanted to talk to someone who had done it; we should have reference customers ready for migration questions.
findings.quote: He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it.
